pullRequest.title: fix: address all unresolved feedback from recent merged PRs

nodes.body:
### Doctor `--dry-run` flag is now dead code **Low Severity** Changing `dryRunInstall` from `opts.dryRun === true && !applyFixes` to `!applyFixes` makes the `--dry-run` CLI option (line 178) completely inert — `opts.dryRun` is never read. Since `dryRunInstall` and `applyFixes` are now strict complements, the `else` branch at lines 250–252 is unreachable dead code. A user passing `--fix --dry-run` would still get mutations applied, contradicting the flag's description. The `--dry-run` option definition could be removed (or `opts.dryRun` actually consulted) to avoid user confusion.
Additional Locations (2) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/verify.ts#L177-L178`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/82826934fe8405d13b4b6292bc7f22144b854fc0/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/verify.ts#L177-L178) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/verify.ts#L247-L252`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/82826934fe8405d13b4b6292bc7f22144b854fc0/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/verify.ts#L247-L252)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 82826934fe8405d13b4b6292bc7f22144b854fc0. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### GraphQL server recreated on every POST request **Medium Severity** Every POST to `/graphql` calls `await import(…)` and `createGraphQLServer(…)`, rebuilding the Yoga schema, resolvers, and plugins from scratch per request. This adds substantial overhead on every GraphQL query to the dashboard, and the server instances are immediately discarded. The recovery checklist item 1318.17 flags this exact issue as TODO but the fix was not applied — the Yoga instance can be created once when the dashboard server starts and reused across requests.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 82826934fe8405d13b4b6292bc7f22144b854fc0. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### `require()` in ESM module crashes at runtime **High Severity** The `cmd-doctor.ts` file uses `require("node:path")` and `require("node:os")` inside the disk space check, but the package is configured as `"type": "module"` in `package.json`. In ESM, `require` is not defined, so this line will throw a `ReferenceError` at runtime, causing the doctor command's disk space check to always fail. The existing top-level ESM imports for `join` from `node:path` are already available but unused here, and `homedir` from `node:os` would need a top-level import or `createRequire`. This is particularly notable because the recovery checklist item 1320.23 specifically called out this exact same bug as unresolved.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Unused `statSync` import in cmd-doctor.ts **Low Severity** `statSync` is imported from `node:fs` but never used anywhere in `cmd-doctor.ts`. This is dead code that the recovery checklist item 1320.21 explicitly flagged as needing removal, yet it persists in this commit.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### `MemoryPluginContext["config"]` resolves to `unknown` type **Medium Severity** `MemoryPluginContext` is defined as `Record`, so `MemoryPluginContext["config"]` resolves to `unknown`. This means the `config` field in `PluginExtensionContext` is typed `unknown`, and `pluginContext.config` at line 140 indexes into an untyped record — likely returning `undefined` at runtime since a plain `Record` won't have a `config` key unless explicitly provided. Plugins receiving `context.config` will get `undefined` rather than meaningful configuration.
Additional Locations (2) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/api/plugin-system.ts#L89-L90`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db/extensions/memory-hybrid/api/plugin-system.ts#L89-L90) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/api/plugin-system.ts#L139-L140`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db/extensions/memory-hybrid/api/plugin-system.ts#L139-L140)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### CORS `origin: "*"` with `credentials: true` is invalid **Medium Severity** The GraphQL Yoga server configures CORS with `origin: "*"` and `credentials: true` simultaneously. Browsers reject `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` when credentials are included — credentialed requests silently fail. This was flagged as checklist item 1318.14 (still `TODO`) but the dashboard now creates and uses this Yoga server instance at startup, making this a live issue for the `/graphql` endpoint.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a60b1e5b32b4dd2e0a2a31b002c2a42f281722db. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Unused `withExit` import in providers command **Low Severity** `withExit` is imported from `./shared.js` but never used anywhere in the file. The recovery checklist item 1320.18 claims the `providers` async action is now "wrapped with `withExit(...)`", but the action at line 14 is still a bare `async () => { ... }` with a manual try/catch. The import is dead code and the stated fix is incomplete.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 95f91dffd6040ba7798c2f244306116dba6a592f. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Doctor disk check ignores configured memory path **Medium Severity** The disk space check hardcodes `join(homedir(), ".openclaw/plugins/memory-hybrid")` instead of reading `cfg.paths?.memory` with a fallback, as the old code did. Users with a custom-configured memory path will get disk space checks on the wrong directory, potentially reporting inaccurate results or false warnings.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 95f91dffd6040ba7798c2f244306116dba6a592f. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Google API key not forwarded to provider detection **Medium Severity** The `detectAvailableProviders` function now accepts a second `googleApiKey` parameter (added to support Google provider detection per item 1320.5), but all CLI callers (`cmd-doctor`, `cmd-health`, `cmd-providers`) only pass `cfg.embedding?.apiKey` without forwarding `cfg.embedding?.googleApiKey`. Users who configure a separate Google API key will see Google reported as unavailable because the fallback uses the OpenAI key, which may be unset.
Additional Locations (2) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-health.ts#L31-L32`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/6b8d0239f2d47c280461e433825635097a6acd35/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-health.ts#L31-L32) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-providers.ts#L17-L18`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/6b8d0239f2d47c280461e433825635097a6acd35/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-providers.ts#L17-L18)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6b8d0239f2d47c280461e433825635097a6acd35. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Unencrypted export files not cleaned up from temp directory **Medium Severity** The sync-export command writes unencrypted fact data to `tmpExportDir` via `runExport` and reads it with `collectExportBundleFiles`, but never cleans up the temp directory afterward. The old code explicitly called `unlinkSync(exportResult.outputPath)` after reading. Sensitive memory content now persists unencrypted in the OS temp directory until the OS eventually purges it.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6b8d0239f2d47c280461e433825635097a6acd35. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

[Bugbot Autofix](https://cursor.com/docs/bugbot#autofix) determined this is a false positive. The cleanup code with rmSync(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) in a finally block is already present at line 2845. You can send follow-ups to the cloud agent here.

### Setup wizard omits Google API key for detection **Medium Severity** The setup wizard calls `detectAvailableProviders(cfg.embedding?.apiKey)` and `recommendProvider(cfg.embedding?.apiKey)` without passing the second `googleApiKey` argument. All other callers in this PR (`cmd-doctor.ts`, `cmd-health.ts`, `cmd-providers.ts`) correctly pass both keys, e.g. `detectAvailableProviders(cfg.embedding?.apiKey, cfg.embedding?.googleApiKey)`. This means the wizard will never detect Google as available or recommend it, despite adding `"google"` as a provider choice on line 84 and handling Google API key input on lines 116–123.
Additional Locations (2) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-setup.ts#L80-L81`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/1501050bed8bd225dbb651d6d89a09ba01e21c5d/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-setup.ts#L80-L81) - [`extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-setup.ts#L86-L87`](https://github.com/markus-lassfolk/openclaw-hybrid-memory/blob/1501050bed8bd225dbb651d6d89a09ba01e21c5d/extensions/memory-hybrid/cli/cmd-setup.ts#L86-L87)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1501050bed8bd225dbb651d6d89a09ba01e21c5d. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### promptHidden permanently patches stdout.write on readline failure **Medium Severity** `promptHidden` replaces `process.stdout.write` globally with a muting wrapper, but only restores it inside the `rl.question` callback. If readline closes before the callback fires (e.g., piped stdin EOF, SIGINT, or stream error), the original `write` is never restored. This leaves `process.stdout` permanently silenced for the rest of the process, and the returned promise never resolves, hanging the CLI.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 41fd617defe392208cdc549d91a84a885bdd60eb. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore subscription argument filtering**

The subscription resolvers now ignore all query arguments and subscribe every client to every event (`category`, `scope`, `factId`, etc. are no longer applied). This regresses behavior promised by the schema and can leak unrelated updates to subscribers that requested a narrower stream, especially in multi-tenant or multi-session usage. Re-introduce per-event predicate filtering in `subscribe` so payloads are scoped to the caller’s arguments.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid resolving hidden prompts to empty string**

`promptHidden` registers an `rl.on("close")` handler that resolves `""`, but the question callback calls `rl.close()` before resolving the typed answer. That means normal interactive entry can resolve to the empty string first, so OpenAI/Google API keys are silently dropped during `setup --interactive`. Resolve only once from the question callback (and keep close handling for abort paths) to avoid losing user input.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect configured memory path in doctor disk check**

The disk-space check now hardcodes `~/.openclaw/plugins/memory-hybrid` and no longer considers `cfg.paths?.memory`. Installations using a custom memory directory will be reported as missing/unhealthy even when storage is valid, which creates false warnings and misleading remediation advice. Use the configured path first and fall back to the default only when unset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail supersede mutation when old fact is missing**

This resolver validates only `newFactId` and ignores the boolean result of `factsDb.supersede(...)`. If `oldFactId` does not exist (or was already superseded), the mutation still returns success with the new fact, so clients get a false positive despite no lineage change. Check that the old fact exists or that `supersede` returns `true`, and throw when the operation did not apply.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop treating OpenAI key as Google provider config**

Google availability is computed with `googleApiKey ?? currentApiKey`, so any configured OpenAI key marks Google as available even when no Google key exists. This produces incorrect provider status/recommendations and can direct users into a non-working Google setup path. Google readiness should depend only on the Google key input.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

ProgressSpinner.success()/fail() no longer emit any completion output (they only stop the spinner and compute unused elapsed variables). This makes setup/doctor flows lose their success/failure feedback, and in non-TTY mode there is now no output at all. Restore a minimal console log (or provide a logger callback) so callers get a completion line even when not in TTY.

statusMessage() has become a no-op (it builds an icons map but never prints), which breaks cmd-demo's final success line and any other CLI status messaging that relies on it. Re-introduce the console output (or route through the project logger) so callers see the intended feedback.

CollaborationService constructor uses `require(...)` in an ESM module, but `require` is not defined in ESM and will throw at runtime. Use `createRequire(import.meta.url)` (as done elsewhere) or switch to a static import from `node:sqlite` so this service can be constructed without crashing.

GraphQL subscription resolvers no longer apply the schema-defined filters (e.g. factCreated(category, scope), factUpdated(factId, category), linkCreated(sourceId, targetId)). The current subscribe() implementations ignore args, so clients requesting filtered subscriptions will receive all events. Reintroduce payload filtering based on the subscription arguments (as before) to match the schema and avoid noisy/unexpected updates.

googleConfigured is computed from `hasConfiguredApiKey(googleApiKey ?? currentApiKey)`, which will mark the Google provider as available whenever an OpenAI apiKey is present (even if no Google/Gemini key is configured). That can mislead setup/providers output and cause recommendProvider() to pick google incorrectly. Compute googleConfigured from googleApiKey only (or an explicit google-specific config source).
